claim: CV reduplication copies the initial CV of the primary-stressed foot, and the resulting stress pattern is monomorpheme-like, indicating that the CV reduplicant is integrated into the root's prosodic word.
normalized_environment: CV RED integrated into root PWd; stress recalculates within same domain
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The CV reduplicant often sounds shorter than an ordinary unstressed syllable, but still counts as moraic. The authors found no vowel-initial verbs undergoing this CV reduplication pattern.

claim: Two-mora reduplication typically copies the primary-stressed foot and behaves as though a prosodic-word boundary separates reduplicant and base, especially when a monomoraic suffix changes the footing of the second copy but not the first.

source_forms.diagnostic: suffix affects base copy footing but not reduplicant footing

formal_environment: two-mora reduplication, especially with following suffixation
normalized_environment: bimoraic RED and base form separate PWd domains
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The authors explicitly note that the crucial examples are few, and some patterns are also compatible with an initial-dactyl preference or partial faithfulness to the unsuffixed form.

claim: Heterosyllabic identical-vowel sequences are licensed across compound boundaries and, in careful speech, do not behave like monomorphemic long vowels: they neither attract stress as long vowels do nor undergo trochaic shortening.
normalized_environment: identical V hiatus preserved across compound PWd boundary in careful speech
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Mosel & Hovdhaugen are cited as giving cases where stress does shift; the authors therefore restrict the categorical diagnostic to their careful-speech data.

claim: When denominal or ergative /-a/ is added to an /a/-final stem, the identical vowels fuse or are at least phonetically indistinguishable from a stressed long vowel, consistent with /-a/ belonging to the stem's prosodic word.
normalized_environment: identical Vs coalesce/behave as long vowel within same PWd
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The authors cannot phonetically determine whether the representation is monosyllabic [áː] or disyllabic [á.a]; the distributional fact is that the sequence behaves unlike compound-boundary ViVi.

claim: Productive ergative /-ina/ forms a separate prosodic word: after an /i/-final stem, the two /i/ vowels remain in separate feet with no fusion or shortening, making stem+-ina pattern like a compound rather than like stem+-a.
normalized_environment: Vi#PWd Vi across stem/-ina boundary; no coalescence or shortening
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This contrasts with unproductive suffixes discussed later, which may fail to project a separate prosodic word.

claim: Diphthong-forming stress disruption is blocked across compound boundaries and across other productive morpheme boundaries that project prosodic-word edges, even when the adjacent vowels would diphthongise monomorphemically.
formal_environment: nonhigh+high VV across compound/productive-morpheme PWd boundary
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Semi-productive and unproductive affixes can fail to project a p-word boundary, yielding different outcomes; productivity is therefore part of the conditioning.

claim: Semi-productive /-Ci/ and unproductive ergative /-ia/ do not consistently initiate a separate prosodic word; the authors interpret this as a productivity-sensitive domain effect in which unproductive affixes may not be parsed as independent morphemes by the phonology.
normalized_environment: low-productivity suffix remains inside stem PWd; no projected left PWd edge
exceptions_or_counterexamples: One /-ia/ item 'shine on-IA' is variable; the authors also stress that evidence is limited to available elicited forms.

claim: In final V1V2V3 sequences, V1V2 shows the ordinary nonhigh+high diphthongising stress pattern when V3 is not /a/, but when V3 is /a/ the diphthongising set broadens to include some low-mid sequences; this produces antepenultimate stress in VVa words beyond the basic VV inventory.
normalized_environment: final a strengthens prominence-mismatch effect and broadens V1V2 stress disruption
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The broadened pattern is restricted to VVa configurations and is analyzed with a separate prominence-mismatch condition; it should not be generalized to all VVV sequences.
